map.多半是类型信息在转换中被保守处理：TOML 有原生日期时间类型，JSON 没有对: Mostly the type info was handled conservatively during conversion: TOML has native datetime types, while JSON has no matching type, so they are usually converted to ISO 8601 strings; also very large integers may be output as strings to avoid precision loss. Consumers must parse per field, especially dates and 64-bit integers.
map.TOML 解析：去回车后逐行处理，跳过空行与 # 注释（# 判定避开引号内部）；: TOML parsing: strip CR and process line by line, skipping blank lines and # comments (# detection avoids quoted regions); [section] builds nested objects level by level on ., and [[array]] appends a new element to the array of that name; other lines split on the first = into key and value, with trailing # comments stripped outside quotes. Value parsing supports double-quoted strings (unescaping \n \t \" \\), single-quoted literal strings, triple-quoted multi-line strings, booleans, integers/floats (underscores and 0x/0o/0b prefixes and scientific notation allowed), [ ] arrays (split on top-level commas, so commas inside quotes and nested levels are preserved) and { } inline tables (recursive key/value); multi-line arrays, inline tables and multi-line strings are accumulated across lines until brackets close; values such as dates/times that JSON cannot represent are kept as strings. JSON output uses tab or the given number of spaces (2 by default) for indentation, and when sorting is enabled keys at every level are reordered lexicographically
